answer: A practical defence is Signed broadband contract age with provider attestation. It rests on a contract held with one provider since 2019, which gives every honest agent a kernel that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since a contract held with one provider since 2019 takes calendar time as well as money — and the marble is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The vertex is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
